Rashi on Chullin 53a:10:1.english: And a claw was found - Detached in [its] back.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:10:2.hebrew: רוב אריות דורסין - כלומר, אע"פ שרוב אריות דורסין, וקים לן שכל הדורס אין לך אחד בהן שתשמט צפרנו:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:10:2.english: A majority of lions claw - That is to say: Even though a majority of lions claw, [nevertheless] it is established for us that [regarding] any [lion] that claws, you do not have a single one among them whose claw is ripped out.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:10:3.hebrew: נתחכך - השור, וצפורן זו בכותל היתה:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:10:3.english: [It] rubbed - The ox [rubbed], and this claw was in the wall.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:12:1.english: Rav [conforms] to his line of reasoning - [As stated] below.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:13:1.hebrew: מקום צפורן - שלא נשמט ולא נמצא שם הצפורן, אלא מקומה ומכתה ניכרת בשור:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:13:1.english: The spot of a claw - Where [a claw] was not ripped out and the claw was not found there, but rather its place and its wound are discernible on the ox.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:13:2.english: Moist - That there was blood in it:

Rashi on Chullin 53a:13:3.english: It is prone to be ripped out - And perhaps [the lion] clawed [it].

Rashi on Chullin 53a:14:1.english: In the row of its paw - That they stand in the back of the ox in the order that they are arranged on the paw of the lion.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:1.hebrew: אימר כלבא - והא אמרינן: אין דרוסה לכלב, דאין לו ארס:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:1.english: Say [it was] a dog - For behold, we say: There is no [halakha of] clawing for a dog, as it has no venom.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:2.english: [If it] entered - A lion [entered] among them and sat there.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:3.hebrew: שלמא שוי - עשה שלום עמהם, כדרך כמה חיות שנעשות תרבות וגדלות עם בני אדם ובהמות, ואין מזיקין:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:3.english: It made peace - It made peace with them, in the manner of various wild animals that become tame and grow up with human beings and domestic animals, and do not cause harm.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:4.hebrew: נח ריתחיה - בהני, ולא חיישינן לדריסה באחריני:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:4.english: Its anger subsided - With these, and we do not suspect clawing among the others.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:6.hebrew: מקרקרין - גועות, דלשון צעקת ארי לחוד ולשון צעקת כל בהמה לחוד, כמו בלשון עברית: נוהם לארי, וגועה לשור, וערוג לאיל, וצהל לסוס, וצפצוף לעופות, וחרץ לכלב:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:16:6.english: Clucking - [They were] lowing. For the term for the cry of a lion is distinct, and the term for the cry of each animal is distinct, just as in the Hebrew language: nohem [roaring] for a lion, go'eh [lowing] for an ox, arog [panting] for a deer, tzahal [neighing] for a horse, tsiftzuf [chirping] for birds, and charatz [snarling] for a dog.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:1:1.hebrew: אף לחולדה - שהיא קטנה הימנו, יש דרוסה, וכ"ש לחתול:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:1:1.english: Even a weasel - For it is smaller than it, [yet] there is [the law of] clawing, and all the more so for a cat.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:1:2.hebrew: אף לחתול - שהוא גדול אין דרוסה, וכ"ש לחולדה. ולקמיה מתרצינן לה:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:1:2.english: Even a cat - Which is large, does not [render an animal a tereifa through] clawing, and all the more so a weasel. And later on we resolve it.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:3:1.hebrew: באימרי רברבי - בבהמה דקה ס"ל אין דרוסה לחתול, כדאמר רב לעיל (חולין דף נב:): בבהמה מן הזאב ולמעלה:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:3:1.english: In adult sheep - He holds [that] for small livestock, a cat has no [power of] clawing, as Rav said above (Chullin 52b): Regarding an animal, [clawing applies only] from a wolf and above.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:3:2.english: In [the case of] kids and lambs - [Which are] very small.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:4:1.english: Other non-kosher birds - Except for the large [bird of prey] and the hawk.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:5:1.hebrew: והא אנן תנן ודרוסת הנץ בעוף הדק - מכלל דשאר עופות, אפילו בעוף הדק — לא:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:5:1.english: But didn’t we learn: “And [what is] clawed by a hawk in a small bird” - By implication, other birds [of prey], even in [the case of] a small bird, do not [render it a tereifa through clawing].

Rashi on Chullin 53a:5:2.hebrew: בדרברבי מיניה - ואפ"ה, עוף הדק הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:5:2.english: In [a bird that is] larger than it - And even so, it is [still considered] a small bird.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:6:1.english: Beit Hini - The name of a place.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:1.english: With the foreleg - That it struck it with its foreleg.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:3.english: But a tooth [does] not - For the venom of the beast is not in its teeth.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:4.hebrew: שלא מדעת - דכיון דשלא מדעת נפל, כגון מן הגג על הבהמה — אע"פ שנתקעה צפרנו בגבה, אין משליך בה ארס:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:4.english: Unintentionally - For since it fell unintentionally, such as from the roof onto the animal, even though its claw became stuck in its back, it does not inject venom into it.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:5.hebrew: לאחר מיתה - קס"ד שמת הארי, ואחר כך נפל על הבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:8:5.english: After death - One might think that the lion died, and afterward fell upon the animal.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:9:1.hebrew: דדריס - מחיים, ולא הספיק לשלוף צפורנו ממנה עד שפסקו את ידו. ומיתה דקאמר — מיתת האבר שנחתך:
Rashi on Chullin 53a:9:1.english: That it clawed - During [its] lifetime, and it did not have time to withdraw its claw from it before they severed its foreleg. And [as for] the “death” that was stated — [it refers to] the death of the limb that was severed.

Rashi on Chullin 53a:9:2.english: [While] it withdraws - When it pulls out and removes its claw from its back.

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:10:1.hebrew: רוב אריות דורסים - וא"ת: אפילו אם תמצא לומר דצפורן זה מחמת חיכוך אתא, מ"מ אפילו בשאר שוורים שאין בהם צפורן היה לנו לחוש, כיון דרוב אריות שבין השוורים דורסין! ובסמוך נמי, דקאמר אביי: "אבל מקום צפורן חיישינן" — למה לי מקום צפורן כלל? ואומר ר"ת דהכי פירושו: "רוב אריות דורסין" — כלומר, ראויין לדרוס, שהן בריאים ודורסים, ומעוטן חולין ואין דורסים; ורוב אריות הדורסים שהם בריאים, אין צפורן נשמטת מהן. וזו, הואיל וצפורן יושבת לו על גבו, מסתמא האי ארי חולה הוא, ולא מחמת דרוסה בא צפורן זה לכאן, אלא בכותל נתחכך; והיה הארי שוכב אצל הכותל, ומחמת שנתחכך השור בכותל וברגלו של ארי, נשמטה ממנו הצפורן וישבה לו על גבו. ופריך: אדרבה, אע"ג דרוב שוורים מתחככין, מ"מ רוב שוורים אין מתחככין במקום שרגל ארי מונחת שם שתשב לו צפורן על גבו, ויש לתלות הצפורן בדריסת הארי, ואע"ג דרוב הבריאים הדורסים אין צפורן נשמטת. ומסיק דאיכא למימר הכי והכי, ורב לטעמיה, דלא חיישינן לספק דרוסה, דאוקמינן אחזקתה קמייתא, בחזקת שלא נדרס:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:10:1.english: "A majority of lions claw" - And if you say: Even if you say that this claw came about due to rubbing [against the wall], nevertheless, even regarding the other oxen that have no claw in them, we should have been concerned [that they were clawed], since a majority of lions that [enter] among oxen claw! And nearby as well, when Abaye says, "However, [if only] the site of a claw [is found], we are concerned" — why do I need [the case of finding] the site of a claw at all? And Rabbeinu Tam says that this is its explanation: "A majority of lions claw" — that is to say, [they] are fit to claw, for they are healthy and claw, and a minority of them are sick and do not claw. And [from] the majority of lions that claw, which are healthy, a claw is not ripped out from them. And as for this [ox], since a claw sits upon its back, presumably this lion is sick, and this claw did not come here due to clawing; rather, [the ox] rubbed against the wall, and the lion was lying next to the wall, and because the ox rubbed against the wall and against the lion's foot, the claw was ripped out from it and settled upon its back. And [the Gemara] objects: On the contrary! Even though a majority of oxen rub [against walls], nevertheless, a majority of oxen do not rub in a place where a lion's foot is lying such that a claw would settle upon its back; and [therefore] one should attribute the claw to the clawing of the lion, even though [from] the majority of healthy [lions] that claw, a claw is not ripped out. And [the Gemara] concludes that one can say this and one can say that, and Rav conforms to his [regular line of] reasoning, that we are not concerned with an uncertainty of clawing (safek derusah), for we establish [the animal] upon its original presumptive status, in the presumption that it was not clawed.

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:10:2.hebrew: כל הדורס אין הצפורן נשמטת - האי "כל" לאו דוקא, וכן "כל המתחכך" דבסמוך; אלא כלומר: רוב הדורסין, רוב המתחכך:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:10:2.english: Any [lion] that claws, the claw is not ripped out - This [use of] "any" is not precise, and likewise "any [ox] that rubs" nearby; rather, it means: a majority of those that claw, [and] a majority of those that rub.

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:1:1.hebrew: יש דרוסה לחתול או לאו כו' - הרב ר' יצחק בר"מ מפרש, דכל הנך בעיות הוי בכמה זימנין: דפעם ראשונה היה עוסק בעופות, ושאלו אם יש דרוסה לחתול, והשיב לו רב: "אפילו לחולדה יש דרוסה". ושוב היה עוסק באימרי רברבי, ושאלו אם יש דרוסה לחולדה אם לאו, והשיב לו: "אפילו לחתול אין דרוסה". ושוב היה עוסק בגדיים וטלאים, ושאלו: חולדה וחתול יש להם דרוסה או לא? וא"ל: לחתול יש דרוסה, ולא לחולדה. וכן היה מפרש ההיא עובדא דשבת פ' תולין (שבת דף קלח. ושם ד"ה בעא): גבי כילה מהו, אמר לו: אף מטה אסורה; מטה מהו, א"ל: אף כילה מותרת; כילה ומטה מהו, א"ל: כילה אסורה ומטה מותרת, ולא קשיא כו'. ועוד י"ל, דכל הנך הוו בפעם אחת: בתחלה שאלו: יש דרוסה לחתול או לאו? א"ל: אתה שואל סתם, יש דבר שאף לחולדה יש דרוסה. והדר בעי מיניה: אם לחולדה יש דרוסה בכל מקום? וא"ל: אף לחתול פעמים שאין דרוסה. והדר בעי מיניה: כיון דזה וזה פעמים יש דרוסה ופעמים שאין דרוסה, שוים הן או לאו? אמר לו: יש דבר דלחתול יש דרוסה, ולחולדה אין דרוסה. וכענין זה יש לפרש ההיא דשבת:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:1:1.english: "Does a cat render [an animal a tereifa] through clawing, or not, etc." - The Rav, Rabbi Yitzchak ben Meir [Ribam], explains that all these inquiries occurred on several [different] occasions: For the first time, he was dealing with birds, and he asked him whether a cat renders [an animal a tereifa] through clawing, and Rav answered him: "Even a weasel renders [it a tereifa] through clawing." And later, he was dealing with large sheep, and he asked him whether a weasel renders [it a tereifa] through clawing or not, and he answered him: "Even a cat does not render [it a tereifa] through clawing." And later, he was dealing with kids and lambs, and he asked him: "Do a weasel and a cat render [them a tereifa] through clawing or not?" and he said to him: "A cat renders [them a tereifa] through clawing, but not a weasel." And he would similarly explain that incident in Shabbat, in the chapter [entitled] Tolin (Shabbat 138a, and there s.v. Ba'a), regarding: "What is [the ruling concerning] a canopy?" He said to him: "Even a bed is forbidden." "What is [the ruling concerning] a bed?" He said to him: "Even a canopy is permitted." "What is [the ruling concerning] a canopy and a bed?" He said to him: "A canopy is forbidden, and a bed is permitted; and this is not difficult, etc." And furthermore, it can be said that all of these [inquiries] took place on one occasion: Initially, he asked him: "Does a cat render [an animal a tereifa] through clawing, or not?" He said to him: "You are asking generally; [yet] there is a case where even a weasel renders [it a tereifa] through clawing." Then he asked him further: "Does a weasel render [it a tereifa] through clawing in all circumstances?" And he said to him: "Even regarding a cat, there are times when it does not render [it a tereifa] through clawing." Then he asked him further: "Since both with this one and with that one there are times when there is clawing and times when there is no clawing, are they equivalent or not?" He said to him: "There is a case where a cat renders [it a tereifa] through clawing, but a weasel does not render [it a tereifa] through clawing." And in a similar manner, that [incident] of Shabbat can be explained.

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:4:1.hebrew: שאר עופות טמאים יש להן דרוסה או אין להן דרוסה - הך דרוסה, היינו דשדי זיהריה כי שליף, ואין זה כי ההיא דלקמן (חולין נט.): "דכל עוף הדורס טמא", דהוי מסימני טומאה. ולא מבעיא ליה הכא אלא בעופות טמאין, אבל פשיטא דאין דרוסה לטהורים:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:4:1.english: "Other non-kosher birds, do they have [the law of] clawing, or do they not have [the law of] clawing?" - This clawing means that it injects its venom when it withdraws [its claws], and this is not like that [statement] later (Chullin 59a): "any bird that claws is non-kosher," which is [one] of the signs of non-kosher status. And he only raised the dilemma here with regard to non-kosher birds, but it is obvious that there is no [halakhic] clawing for kosher [birds].

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:6:1.hebrew: ובא מעשה לפני חכמים ואמרו יש דרוסה - וא"ת: ולישני ליה דהכא רחל קטנה היתה, ורב כהנא איירי באימרי רברבי? וי"ל: דא"כ, מאי איריא דנקט רב כהנא שועל? אפילו חתול נמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:6:1.english: "And the incident came before the Sages, and they said: [This] is a case of clawing" - And if you say: But let him answer him that here it was a small ewe, whereas Rav Kahana was dealing with large sheep? And one can say: If so, why did Rav Kahana specifically mention a fox? Even a cat as well [does not claw large sheep]!

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:7:1.hebrew: ובא מעשה לפני חכמים ואמרו אין דרוסה - וא"ת: ולישני ליה דהכא רחל גדולה היתה, וכן משמע מדלא נקט טלה? וי"ל: דא"כ, לא הוה רב דימי משמיענו שום חדוש בהאי מעשה, דאפילו לחתול אין דרוסה ברברבי:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:7:1.english: "And the incident came before the Sages, and they said: [This is] not [a case of] clawing" - And if you say: Let him answer that here it was a large ewe, and so it is implied from [the fact] that he did not say "a lamb"? And one can say: For if so, Rav Dimi would not have been teaching us any novelty in this incident, for even regarding a cat there is no [rule of] clawing in large [animals].

Tosafot on Chullin 53a:9:1.hebrew: קא משמע לן דבהדי דשליף שדי זיהריה - יש שטועין להתיר לשחוט כשהנץ שוכב ע"ג העוף ולא הסיר רגליו עדיין, דאכתי לא שליף ולא שדי ביה זיהריה. ואסור לעשות כן, דכשהנץ רודף אחר העוף ולוכדו, מכהו כמה פעמים ברגליו, ודריס ושליף כמה זימנין:
Tosafot on Chullin 53a:9:1.english: It teaches us that while it withdraws, it injects its venom - There are those who mistakenly permit slaughtering [a bird] when the hawk is lying on top of the bird and has not yet removed its feet, [reasoning] that it has not yet withdrawn [its claws] and has not injected its venom into it. But it is forbidden to do so, because when the hawk pursues the bird and catches it, it strikes it several times with its feet, and claws and withdraws [them] multiple times.
